question: Does preventing silent draw-branch extinction during final compression reduce high-confidence direction misses at matched ticket cost?
hypothesis: When a draw state remains visible in the pre-compression CRS candidate layer and is supported by the corresponding TTG total, preserving at least one draw state for review can reduce final-compression information loss.
baseline: Existing final-compression output without a draw-preservation review request
treatment: Draw Branch Preservation Gate v0.1 shadow review

reject_or_keep_shadow_if: The gate only increases selection count/cost without reducing high-confidence misses.
Any apparent improvement disappears after matched-cost comparison.
The effect is confined to a single short window or league.
The gate is tuned after outcomes using unfrozen thresholds.
The retained draw branch is chosen post-hoc rather than from pre-match frozen states.
ROI improvement comes with materially worse drawdown outside preregistered tolerance.
